messages:
Acme SRE: Hey team, our Private deployment (vpc-prod-011) suddenly started failing for inference calls ~10:10am UTC. Client gets "TLS handshake timeout" or sometimes "connection refused". No config changes on our side. Can you help?
Maya Chen: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl/SDK error and whether this is in a single AZ?
Acme SRE: curl -v https://inference.internal.redwood.acme:443 returns:
```
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to inference.internal.redwood.acme (10.10.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection attempt failed: handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake timeout
```
We're in us-east-1a, behind a NAT gateway; SGs are pretty locked down.
Leo Park: Can you confirm the SGs and NACL rules around the worker subnet? Common issue is NACL blocking ephemeral ports so return SYN-ACKs don't get back.
Acme SRE: SG outbound allows 443 to 35.XXX.XXX.0/24 (your control plane IPs), inbound from our app subnet only. NACL inbound/outbound rules are fairly strict, only allowing 80,443, 10250 (kube), plus a couple CIDR entries.
Maya Chen: Two quick repro checks: 1) run `curl -vk` to see TLS details, 2) from the instance run `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443 or portrange 1024-65535` while you curl and paste output. That will show if SYNs get a SYN-ACK.
Acme SRE: Ran tcpdump during a failed curl, here's the snippet:
```
10:12:01.123456 IP 10.10.4.12.40012 > 10.10.5.23.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
10:12:06.123789 IP 10.10.4.12.40012 > 10.10.5.23.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [...], length 0
(no SYN-ACKs)
```
Leo Park: That indicates we never got a SYN-ACK back — likely the reply is being dropped (NACL or stateful device missing). NACLs are stateless; if you only allow inbound 443 but not outbound ephemeral ports, return traffic will be dropped. What are your NACL entries?
Acme SRE: NACL (subnet-workers):
- rule 100 allow TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 inbound
- rule 110 allow TCP 80 0.0.0.0/0 inbound
- rule 120 allow TCP 443 10.0.0.0/8 outbound
- rule 130 deny all / default -1
We thought SG stateful would be enough.
Maya Chen: Aha. Two things to explain: Security Groups are stateful — if SG allows outbound, return traffic is allowed. NACLs are stateless and need symmetric rules for both directions. For TLS connections from your app instances to our nodes you need to allow ephemeral port range (1024-65535) in the NACL outbound (so that the remote side can reply to your source port) and inbound for established flows depending on how you defined direction. Example recommended NACL entries: allow ephemeral ports outbound (1024-65535) to 0.0.0.0/0 and allow ephemeral inbound if you expect remote-initiated flows.
Ryan O'Neill: Also check NAT/GW or egress ACL on the transit. If you use a NAT gateway, the NAT will source-port translate; but NACL still applies at the subnet boundary. Another gotcha: AWS NACLs are evaluated by rule number order; a broad deny with a lower rule number will shadow later allows.
Acme SRE: Ok we added outbound rule allow TCP 1024-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0 (rule 115) and moved deny all to 200. Retried curl.
Acme SRE: After the change curl now returns TLS handshake progressing further, but the SDK still sees intermittent failures for streaming endpoints (long-lived). Logs show a few resets.
Maya Chen: For streaming we also rely on long-lived connections — ensure idle timeouts on any LB/NAT are high enough. What LB are you fronting with?
Acme SRE: We have a private ALB in the VPC that forwards to worker nodes, idle timeout at 60s.
Leo Park: ALB default idle is 60s — streaming may need 300s. Increase ALB idle timeout and confirm keepalive on the client SDK. Also check any firewall appliance rules for TCP RST on long connections.
Acme SRE: Increased ALB idle to 300s and bumped NACL ephemeral rules to ensure symmetric inbound/outbound. Re-tested with SDK streaming and long prompts — looks stable now.
Maya Chen: Great. Summary we should capture for other customers: 1) Ensure NACLs allow ephemeral port range (1024-65535) outbound/inbound as needed. 2) Use stateful SGs for typical app egress; be aware NACLs are stateless and evaluated by rule order. 3) For long-lived streaming, ensure ALB/NAT/egress proxies have sufficiently long idle timeouts and keepalive configured. 4) If TLS handshake fails, tcpdump to check whether SYN-ACKs are returned or if TLS errors occur after handshake.
infra-bot: Note saved as KB-3827 (Private VPC: NACL ephemeral ports + ALB idle timeout cause for TLS/streaming failures). :white_check_mark:
Acme SRE: Thanks everyone, that KB helped a lot. :pray:
Maya Chen: Glad it's resolved. If you want we'll run a short healthcheck script that verifies your egress to our control plane and streaming endpoints and post it to the KB.
Acme SRE: Please do — would be useful.
Maya Chen: I'll attach a small script to KB-3827 later today. :thumbsup:
